observations.observation: TrendForce’s 29 September release gives a 2027 HBM blended-ASP forecast of +121% YoY, attributing the revision to tight supply, a higher-priced HBM4 mix, and HBM4e ramping in 2H27. The figure is a forecast for a blended product mix, not a realized price or a like-for-like price change for every HBM product.
observations.event_time: 2026-09-29 (release date; intraday time not stated on the official page)
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The public release does not disclose the underlying forecast model, prior numerical estimate, or sensitivity assumptions. MoneyDJ repeats the TrendForce estimate rather than supplying an independent forecast.

observations.observation: TrendForce described GPU and ASIC vendors as considering lower HBM capacity per device and 8-Hi as a priority for evaluation in 2027. Its wording is prospective and does not establish final platform specifications, mass production, or sustained shipments.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: TrendForce’s 4 August page had already reported configuration evaluations and explicitly said Rubin Ultra’s final specification was undetermined; the 29 September passage is not confirmation that a design change was finalized.

observations.observation: A TrendForce bulletin page dated 22 September had already summarized a raised 2027 HBM outlook and said 8-Hi was expected to lead shipments. The 29 September release adds the explicit 121% blended-ASP figure and 10–20% per-Gb 8-Hi premium in its public account.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The 22 September page is a research landing-page summary and does not expose underlying tables or establish when the exact 121% number first became public.

observations.observation: TrendForce’s 29 September account says 8-Hi uses fewer DRAM dies and can reduce stack and GPU bill-of-materials cost, but the fixed base-die cost is spread across less DRAM capacity, yielding an estimated 10–20% higher price per Gb than 12-Hi. It also says lower configurations may support more GPUs from the same HBM bit output.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: These are TrendForce’s cost and market projections; the release provides no observed platform-level procurement prices or realized shipment mix.

observations.observation: MoneyDJ’s timestamped report at 07:25:08Z on 29 September shows the claims had a separate media dissemination before the cutoff. The official TrendForce page itself provides only a calendar date, so the exact ordering of its release versus that report cannot be established from the page timestamp alone.
observations.publication_time: MoneyDJ: 2026-09-29T07:25:08Z; TrendForce official page: 2026-09-29, intraday time unknown
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: MoneyDJ attributes the substance to TrendForce; it is evidence of dissemination, not separate verification.

gaps: The exact intraday publication and revision time of TrendForce’s 29 September official page is not stated; only the supplied pre-cutoff capture verifies that its current passage was present by 08:04:41Z.
No independently sourced customer, GPU/ASIC vendor, or memory supplier confirmation of finalized 8-Hi platform specifications or sustained shipments was verified in the sources reviewed.

The 121% estimate’s underlying model, previous numerical forecast, contract data, and assumptions are not available in the public summary; MoneyDJ repeats the same attribution rather than independently corroborating it.

The 22 September TrendForce report summary shows that the directional outlook predated the 29 September release, but the available page does not establish whether the exact 121% figure was already disclosed then.
research_notes: Evidence is limited to material published by the 2026-09-29T08:08:53.180822Z cutoff. TrendForce’s official release is dated 29 September but has no intraday publication or revision time; the supplied source capture at 08:04:41Z contains the same passage as the live page. MoneyDJ’s separate article timestamp converts to 07:25:08Z (Asia/Taipei, UTC+8), before cutoff, but it attributes its claims to TrendForce rather than independently validating them. Earlier TrendForce pages show that both tight-supply expectations and lower-HBM configuration evaluations predated the 29 September release.
